svg.title: Structures & states
svg.desc: Solid → liquid → gas: Solid: fixed arrangement, vibration. Liquid: close particles move past one another. Gas: widely spaced, rapid random motion. Melting/freezing; boiling/condensing. Heating transfers energy; changes of state are physical. Read melting & boiling data: Below melting point → solid. Between melting and boiling → liquid. Above boiling → gas. State symbols: (s), (l), (g), (aq). Aqueous means dissolved in water. Particles are not hard identical spheres: models omit forces, size differences and continuous movement. Metals conduct & bend: Strong attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons → giant metallic structure. Electrons move and carry charge and transfer energy. Metal layers slide while metallic bonding remains. Alloys resist bending: An alloy mixes a metal with other elements. Different-sized atoms distort regular layers. Layers slide less easily → alloy is harder. Use a labelled particle drawing to explain, not just “stronger”. Polymer chains: Many atoms joined by strong covalent bonds in long molecules. Forces act between chains. Intermolecular forces are usually sufficient for polymers to be solid at room temperature. A repeating unit in brackets with n represents many linked units. Recognise giant structures: Diamond, graphite and silicon dioxide are giant covalent. Many strong bonds need much energy to break → high melting. Contrast small molecules: melting/boiling does not break their internal covalent bonds. Use diagrams, formulae and melting/conductivity data together to identify structure.

g.text: Layers can slide past each other
